newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM gives Mother Teresa get-well bouquet.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM gives Mother Teresa get-well bouquet.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda visited ailing Mother Teresa in hospital on Tuesday with a get-well bouquet of roses.
Deve Gowda washed his hands and took off his shoes in a disinfection process before he entered the critical care unit where the 86-year-old nun is being treated.
She received him sitting in a chair by her bed, and asked him to sit beside her. "She is doing better," Deve Gowda told reporters after the 10-minute meeting.
"I gave her roses and she gave me love and affection."
Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said Mother Teresa, recovering from heart surgery and pneumonia, appeared "a little better" in an update on her condition.

Dr D.P. Shetty, the head of the medical team, quoted the prime minister as telling her he had earmarked a plot of land in the southern city of Bangalore for her Missionaries of Charity religious order to build a home for AIDS patients.
"You have built a house in all of our hearts," Shetty quoted Gowda as saying after he told her the news.
Earlier on Tuesday, the hospital said the nun had had breathing problems about 2.30 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday).
"It lasted for a few minutes and she was put on an oxygen mask," the medical bulletin said. "She is all right now. She had her morning tea around 7.45 a.m. and her prayer."
Last month, Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had surgery to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.
Her recovery has been complicated by her irregular heartbeat, as well as lung and kidney problems.
On Monday, doctors gave her a second mild electric shock in six days to correct a faltering heartbeat. They said the procedure, called cardioversion, was a success.
"Her cardiovascular status seems fairly stable today," the medical bulletin said, adding that "her rhythm remains regular. Pulmonary condition (is) somewhat improved".
But bronchitis, which has dogged Mother Teresa since her youth, continued to worry the doctors.

Hospital staff are helping the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner do simple deep breathing exercises to help relax her throat and chest muscles and keep fluid from collecting in her lungs, the doctors said. They also massage her chest every five hours.
Mother Teresa, who has been asking doctors to let her go home, called her office on Monday evening and playfully asked the sisters there to send an ambulance to pick her up, doctors said.
Doctors hope she will be well enough to go home for Christmas, but they have warned that her recovery will be slow and that she might never be as active as before.
